GettingStarted.title: Connect your AWS account
GettingStarted.subtitle: Read-only, revocable at any time, and nothing leaves your infrastructure.

role.title: IAM role
role.description: A read-only role created by CloudFormation. OpsWatch assumes it with temporary credentials and an ExternalId.

ambient.title: Running on AWS
ambient.description: OpsWatch runs on ECS or EC2 in the account it reads and uses its task or instance role.

keys.title: Access keys
keys.description: Paste a key pair for a quick local test. Easy, but long-lived keys are a risk in production.

diagram.title: How it works
diagram.hint: Hover over or focus a box to see what it does.

account.label: Your AWS account
account.description: The account OpsWatch reads. Nothing is installed in it except one IAM role.

stack.label: CloudFormation stack
stack.description: Generated by OpsWatch for this connection. Deleting the stack removes the role and revokes access.

role.label: IAM role OpsWatchReadOnly
role.description: The only resource the stack creates. It has no password and no keys; it can only be assumed.

permissions.label: Permissions policy
permissions.description: What the role may do: describe and list ECS, ELB, RDS, Performance Insights and CloudWatch, and run Logs Insights queries. No S3, no secrets.

trust.label: Trust policy + ExternalId
trust.description: Who may assume the role: only OpsWatch's identity, and only when it presents this connection's ExternalId.

instance.label: OpsWatch instance
instance.description: Your self-hosted OpsWatch. It has its own AWS identity, allowed only to assume OpsWatch roles.

assumeRole.label: sts:AssumeRole
assumeRole.description: OpsWatch asks AWS STS for access, presenting the role ARN and the ExternalId. AWS checks the trust policy.

credentials.label: Temporary credentials (1 h)
credentials.description: STS returns credentials valid for one hour. OpsWatch renews them automatically and never stores them.

s0.title: Give OpsWatch an AWS identity
s0.body: OpsWatch needs its own identity to assume roles. On a laptop, create an IAM user with only the policy below and give its keys to OpsWatch through AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or an AWS profile. On ECS or EC2, attach the same policy to the task or instance role.

s1.title: Create the connection
s1.body: In OpsWatch, add an account and choose IAM role. OpsWatch generates a unique ExternalId and a CloudFormation template for this connection.

s2.title: Deploy the stack
s2.body: In the account to read, deploy the template: upload it in the CloudFormation console, run the AWS CLI command shown on the connection page, or use Launch Stack when a template bucket is configured.

s3.title: Paste the role ARN
s3.body: When the stack is complete, copy its RoleArn output and paste it on the connection page.

s4.title: Run the test
s4.body: OpsWatch assumes the role and checks each service. Green means allowed, orange means a permission is missing and tells you what you lose, red means the connection failed.

s1.title: Attach the read-only permissions
s1.body: Give the ECS task role or EC2 instance profile the actions listed in "What each service needs", in the account OpsWatch runs in.

s2.title: Create the connection
s2.body: Add an account, choose Running on AWS, and run the test.

s1.title: Create a dedicated IAM user
s1.body: Create a user with only the actions listed in "What each service needs", then create an access key for it.

s2.title: Paste the keys
s2.body: Add an account, choose Access keys and paste the key pair. OpsWatch encrypts it and never shows it again.

s3.title: Rotate or remove
s3.body: Delete the key in IAM when you are done testing, or switch to an IAM role.

GettingStarted.servicesIntro: The role is deliberately narrower than the AWS ReadOnlyAccess policy, which can read the content of S3 buckets. OpsWatch never reads S3, Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store.

serviceCards.billed: {action} is billed by AWS per GB of logs scanned.

ecs.why: List clusters, services and tasks, and read their definitions.
ecs.unlocks: The containers view: services, tasks, deployments and events.

ec2.why: Read instances, network interfaces, security groups and subnets.
ec2.unlocks: Mapping IP addresses and hosts back to services.
ec2.without: IP addresses in logs and database connections stay anonymous.

autoscaling.why: Read the scaling targets and policies of ECS services.
autoscaling.unlocks: Minimum, maximum and target values next to each service.

elb.why: Read load balancers, listeners, rules and target health.
elb.unlocks: Which service receives which traffic, and unhealthy targets.
elb.without: Routing and target health are missing.

rds.why: Read clusters, instances, proxies and events.
rds.unlocks: The databases view, with the real writer and reader roles.

pi.why: Read Performance Insights load, dimensions and SQL text.
pi.unlocks: Top SQL, wait events and the busiest client hosts.
pi.without: You see the CPU but not which query causes it.

cloudwatch.why: Read metric data, list metrics and alarms.
cloudwatch.unlocks: Every chart: CPU, memory, requests, latency and errors.

logs.why: List log groups and run Logs Insights queries.
logs.unlocks: Log search and analyses such as errors per route or the busiest clients.

security.title: Security
security.can1: Read the metadata and metrics of the services listed above.
security.can2: Run the Logs Insights queries you start, which AWS bills.
security.cannot1: Change, create or delete anything in your account.
security.cannot2: Read S3 objects, secrets or parameters.
security.cannot3: Be used by another OpsWatch instance, thanks to the ExternalId.
security.externalIdBody: Without it, anyone who learns your role ARN could configure their own OpsWatch to use it. This is known as the confused deputy problem. The role only accepts requests that also present the random value generated for your connection.
security.revokeBody: Delete the CloudFormation stack. The role disappears and OpsWatch loses access immediately. Then remove the connection in OpsWatch.

assumeRole.title: AccessDenied when assuming the role
assumeRole.body: The trust policy does not match: the stack was deployed from an older template, the ExternalId was regenerated, or OpsWatch now runs with another identity. Download the template again and update the stack.

region.title: A region always fails
region.body: The region may be disabled for your account. Enable it in the AWS account settings, or remove it from the connection.

pi.title: Performance Insights is "not applicable"
pi.body: No instance in that region has Performance Insights enabled. Enable it on the database instance to get the top SQL.

scp.title: A permission stays missing although the role has it
scp.body: A service control policy (SCP) of your AWS organization or a permissions boundary may deny the action. Ask your organization administrator.

account.title: The credentials belong to another account
account.body: The role ARN or the keys come from another AWS account than the one entered for the connection. Check the 12-digit account ID.
